title: HC gives Telangana 8 weeks to bring a lift safety Bill

slides.head: HC gives Telangana 8 weeks to bring a lift safety Bill
What happened
slides.body: In a suo motu PIL, the High Court on Tuesday told the Chief Secretary to expedite the elevator safety law and place the draft Bill before Cabinet within eight weeks.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The court registered the case from letters flagging no legal framework for lift safety; accidents include the death of a police battalion commandant last year, allegedly due to poor maintenance.

slides.head: deadline to reach Cabinet
slides.body: Petitioners' draft rules were already with the government; the file has only reached the Industries department so far.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Government counsel said the process was likely to take another two months.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether the draft Elevator Safety Bill reaches Cabinet inside the eight-week window. Ask: Who checks lift maintenance in apartment blocks today?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
HC gives Telangana 8 weeks to bring a lift safety Bill

A bench of Acting CJ Sam Koshy and Justice Chalapathi Rao directed the Chief Secretary to speed up the long-delayed Elevator Safety Bill for multi-storey buildings.

Why it matters: The court registered the case from letters flagging no legal framework for lift safety; accidents include the death of a police battalion commandant last year, allegedly due to poor maintenance.
